correctness.rationale: For integers free of prime (r+1) powers, factorwise monotonicity maximizes sigma(n)/n at first k primes with exponent r for given omega(n)=k. Mertens/PNT give restricted Gronwall limsup lambda_r=1/zeta(r+1), achieved by primorial powers P_k^r. The moving finite exponential B_c=e^gamma e^x P(Poisson(x)<=floor(x+c sqrt x)) tends to e^gamma loglog(n) Phi(c), yielding limsup lambda_r/Phi(c). At c_r=Phi^-1(lambda_r), the lattice Edgeworth expansion gives phi(c_r)/sqrt(x)*((4-c_r^2)/6 - fractional_phase)+O_r(1/x) on extremal powers; small phase mesh gives both signs if r<=4, while c_r>2 for r>=5 makes the bracket negative. Independent Poisson CDF checks at x=500,2000,10000 and exact numerical quantile signs for r=1..9 support the lattice coefficient/cutoff. The asymptotic uniformity and infinitely many phases use prime-number-theorem and local expansion, not numerical sampling.
